land.text: Old Calabar, whose chiefs 'placed themselves under British protection in 1884'; headquarters of the Niger Coast Protectorate 1884-1906

successors.note: In 1903 the British agreed with the Efik kings to replace the title King with Obong of Calabar; traditional rulers are still recognised.

capitals.name: Akwa Akpa (Old Calabar)
capitals.note: The gazetteer's Calabar point; Duke Town 'believed to have been founded in about 1650'; the infobox names Atakpa.

correction.text: the Efik city-states of Akwa Akpa (Duke Town, Creek Town) on the Calabar river

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area or extent; a 25 km circle round Calabar stands for the Efik towns.

region.text: Akwa Akpa on the Calabar river

ledger.note: c. 1650: Duke Town is founded. 'Dukes Town is believed to have been founded in about 1650 according to historians Ekei Essien Oku and Efiong U. Aye'; the Efik 'had become a power on the coast of the Bight of Biafra by the early 18th century'.

1884: the Calabar chiefs accept British protection. 'The chiefs of Akwa Akpa placed themselves under British protection in 1884.' 'From 1884 until 1906 Old Calabar was the headquarters of the Niger Coast Protectorate.'
1884: the independent Efik city-states end; the Obong of Calabar title replaced King in 1903.

sources.title: Old Calabar
sources.note: Duke Town about 1650; a power by the early 18th century; British protection in 1884; headquarters of the Niger Coast Protectorate 1884-1906; Eyamba 1834-1847; Obong title 1903; no infobox dates, no area.

notes: Old Calabar has no Cliopatria row. One page opened (small state, budget 1-2); no area, no extent beyond the town, no month for the 1884 treaty. The Efik city-states (Duke Town, Creek Town, Henshaw Town, Old Town) are one dossier because the page treats them together; the circle is a stand-in. Rulers: the page has a rulers list in part (Eyamba 1834-1847, Adam Ephraim 1901-1906) but the extract is not a complete list with reign years, so none is given.
